sections.heading: Adverbs with -mente
sections.body:
Add *-mente* (like English "-ly") to the **feminine** form of the adjective: *rápido → rápidamente*, *tranquilo → tranquilamente*, *lento → lentamente*. Adjectives without a feminine form just add it: *fácil → fácilmente*, *normal → normalmente*, *feliz → felizmente*. The written accent stays: *rápidamente, fácilmente*.

Two in a row? Only the last one gets *-mente*: *Habló clara y lentamente.* (She spoke clearly and slowly.)

In conversation, people often use *con* + noun or the adjective itself: *con cuidado* (carefully), *Habla rápido* (He talks fast).

sections.heading: Focus words
sections.body:
- *solo / solamente* (only): *Solo quiero un café.* (No accent on *solo* is the current norm.)
- *sobre todo* (above all, especially): *Me gusta la fruta, sobre todo el mango.*
- *especialmente, precisamente* (precisely), *exactamente*: *Eso es exactamente lo que quería.*

sections.heading: The absolute superlative: -ísimo
sections.body:
To say "very, very" or "extremely", add *-ísimo / -ísima* to the adjective (dropping a final vowel): *caro → carísimo*, *bueno → buenísimo*, *grande → grandísimo*, *fácil → facilísimo*, *rico → riquísimo* (spelling change), *largo → larguísimo*, *poco → poquito / poquísimo*. *La comida estaba riquísima.* (The food was delicious.) *Es una película larguísima.*

It works with some adverbs too: *muchísimo* (very much), *tardísimo* (really late), *cerquita* (very close — a diminutive, common in Latin America).

examples: We walked calmly along the beach.
I really don't know what to do.
Me gusta la fruta, sobre todo el mango.
Eso es exactamente lo que quería.
Normalmente me levanto a las siete.
I normally get up at seven.

exercises.explain: Use the feminine form, and keep the accent.
